newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Agrium to build Argentine fertilizer plant.
newsitem.headline: Agrium to build Argentine fertilizer plant.

text.p: Canada's Agrium International will have a one-third stake in a $600 million fertilizer plant to be built in Argentina to feed the country's booming farm sector, a firm spokeswoman said Friday.
Agrium's partners, also with 33.3-percent stakes, will be Argentine oil firms YPF and Perez Companc, the spokeswoman told Reuters.
The plant's location is still not decided but could be in the southern Buenos Aires province port of Bahia Blanca. It will be built over two-and-a-half years from the end of 1997.

Agrium, which has high hopes for fertilizer demand in Argentina and the region, is also considering installing another large fertilizer plant in San Lorenzo, Santa Fe province. The firm is considering another partnership with YPF and Perez Companc for the second plant, as well as for fertilizer ventures in Brazil.
Fertilizer use has boomed in Argentina in recent years, as local farmers have striven to modernize.
